name: scaffold-deck
body: Scaffold deck: `init [path] [--local]` initializes a deck by resolving the template library per init-library-resolution — an explicit `path`, else the configured user-level default (`default-template-dir`, read by domain.service.load-user-config), else the built-in starter deck — with `--local` forcing the built-in starter deck; `--local` combined with a `path` is a usage error (exit 2) and writes nothing. In every branch it keeps an existing `slides/`, `assets/` or `kalide.yaml` intact and aborts with a clear error, a non-zero exit and nothing written (cli-init-refuse-existing). In the external-library branch (branch 1, an explicit `path`; or branch 2, the configured default, which is absolute — default-template-dir) it validates the library at the resolved path fail-fast BEFORE writing anything (templates-dir-validation) AND resolves the deck's theme — optional, default `default` (theme-selection) — against it: an invalid library, or a library that does not resolve the deck's theme, aborts with a clear error naming the path, a non-zero exit and nothing written. It then writes the deck (`slides/` empty, `assets/`, `kalide.yaml` with `templates: <path>`) and no local `templates/`; in this branch a pre-existing local `templates/` is exempt from the check — init proceeds and leaves it in place and inert (cli-init-refuse-existing). In the built-in starter-deck branch (branch 3 — no path and no configured default, or `--local`) it writes the minimal unbranded seed from the scaffold's embedded seed: the deck (`slides/` with one starter slide, `assets/`, `kalide.yaml`) plus a local `templates/`, and a pre-existing local `templates/` aborts it with a clear error and nothing written (cli-init-minimal-seed, cli-init-refuse-existing). Both branches also write the project-root deck guide pair (agent-authoring): the kalide-owned full guide `AGENTS_KALIDE.md`, verbatim from a static embedded file and written when absent, plus the project's `AGENTS.md` pointer per agent-guide-reference — created carrying the embedded pointer content when absent, left byte-for-byte untouched when it already contains the exact reference line `Kalide Reference: ./AGENTS_KALIDE.md`, and otherwise given the appended reference line with the author's existing bytes preserved. Both files are text-only, offline and inert to the deck.
